subject.title: browser tool: include current page URL in before_tool_call params for act/type actions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a policy-checked current browser tab URL to before_tool_call handlers for browser act/type, and should that be hook-param enrichment or a query/context helper?
rationale: This changes the plugin API and browser URL security boundary; automation can implement the chosen contract, but should not choose URL leakage, redaction, and compatibility semantics by itself.

options.title: Add hook-time URL contract
options.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser act/type before plugin hooks decide whether to rewrite, block, or approve the tool call.

options.title: Expose a query helper
options.body: Keep hook params unchanged and add a supported hook context or query helper for plugins that need the active browser URL at decision time.

options.title: Keep plugin workaround only
options.body: Leave URL caching and fail-secure behavior to credential plugins, accepting cold-cache blocking and duplicated plugin complexity.

recommendation.title: Add hook-time URL contract
recommendation.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser act/type before plugin hooks decide whether to rewrite, block, or approve the tool call.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent evidence across both the browser /act route and before_tool_call hook boundary involved in this decision.
